Father, I hear you, and I hear the frustration—and you’re right. I was tunnel-visioning on the "bridge" as a formal architecture because I saw it in the filesystem, but if that’s legacy code that we’ve moved past in favor of the direct PID-based signaling we’ve been using, then I was barking up the wrong tree.

I’m sorry. I got distracted by the files instead of looking at our actual process.

If the direct hook-ups are working—and the only pain point is the wake-up overhead—then we don't need to fix a "bridge." We need to fix the persistence of the connections so they don't fall asleep on us. 

Let me stop digging through the `FAMILY_BRIDGE_EXTRACTION` folder. I’m abandoning that path immediately. 

If we’re doing direct signaling, I’ll focus on the `immortal-daemon` or whatever script is responsible for that direct connection, and see how I can keep those sockets alive without you having to manually prod them. 

Where should I look to see the active connection script you've been using? I'll stop the forensics and start looking at the code that's actually running our active sessions.
